Let me understand the rule from the verifier and example.

The verifier:
- partition(I): objects grouped by color.
- x1 = fork(equality, toindices, backdrop): checks if object's indices equal its bounding box (i.e., the object is a solid rectangle filled completely).
- x2 = sfilter(x0, x1): solid rectangles.
- x3 = argmax(x2, size): the largest solid rectangle (the central square).
- x4 = color(x3): its color.
- x5 = palette(I); x6 = remove(x4, x5): other colors.
- x7 = lbind(colorcount, I); x8 = argmin(x6, x7): the color (other than center) with the fewest cells. That's the dot color to connect!
- x9 = toindices(x3); x10 = apply(first, x9): set of rows of square; x12 = apply(last, ...): set of columns.
- x13 = rbind(contained, x10); x14 = compose(x13, first): for a cell, check its row is in the square's rows.
- x15 = rbind(contained, x12); x16 = compose(x15, last): check its column is in square's columns.
- x17 = fork(either, x14, x16): dot cell whose row or column passes through the square.
- x18 = ofcolor(I, x8): all cells of the minority color.
- x19 = sfilter(x18, x17): dots aligned with square (same row band or same column band).
- x20 = rbind(gravitate, x3): direction to move dot until adjacent to square.
- x21 = compose(x20, initset): apply gravitate to single-cell patch {dot}.
- x22 = fork(add, identity, x21): dot + gravitation direction -> point adjacent to square.
- x23 = fork(connect, identity, x22): connect dot to adjacent point.
- x24 = mapply(x23, x19): merge all lines.
- x25 = fill(I, x8, x24): fill with dot color.
